title: Decimals (Intro)
description: Class 4 IMO — Introduction to decimals: tenths and hundredths, decimal place value, converting fractions to decimals, comparing decimals, and adding and subtracting decimals.

topics.title: Tenths, Hundredths & Place Value
topics.concept:
A decimal shows parts of a whole using a decimal point. The first digit after the point is tenths (0.1 = 1/10) and the second is hundredths (0.01 = 1/100).

In 3.45 there are 3 ones, 4 tenths and 5 hundredths. So 3.45 = 3 + 0.4 + 0.05.

examples.problem: In 2.45, what does the digit 4 stand for?
examples.solution: 4 is in the tenths place, so it stands for 0.4 (four-tenths).

recap: First decimal place = tenths; second = hundredths.

quiz.q: In 5.62, the digit 2 is in the ___ place.
quiz.explanation: The second digit after the point is hundredths.

topics.title: Fractions to Decimals & Comparing
topics.concept:
A fraction with denominator 10 or 100 is easy to write as a decimal: 3/10 = 0.3 and 45/100 = 0.45. Also ½ = 5/10 = 0.5.

To compare decimals, compare the whole-number part first, then the tenths, then the hundredths. So 0.5 is greater than 0.45 because 5 tenths beats 4 tenths.

examples.solution: 0.7 = 0.70, and 70 hundredths > 65 hundredths, so 0.7 is bigger.

recap: Denominator 10 → one decimal place; 100 → two places.
Compare wholes, then tenths, then hundredths.

quiz.explanation: 0.8 is 8 tenths, far bigger than 0.08 (8 hundredths).

topics.title: Adding & Subtracting Decimals
topics.concept:
To add or subtract decimals, line up the decimal points so tenths sit under tenths and hundredths under hundredths, then add or subtract as usual.

For example, 0.5 + 0.25 = 0.75, and 2.5 − 1.25 = 1.25.
recap: Line up the decimal points before adding or subtracting.
Fill missing places with zeros if needed (2.5 = 2.50).

questions.q: Which is the odd one out (three equal 0.5)?
questions.explanation: 0.05 is 5 hundredths, not a half; the other three equal 0.5.

questions.q: In 4.56, what is the value of the digit 5?
questions.explanation: 5 is in the tenths place, so it stands for 0.5.

questions.q: A ribbon of 0.5 m is joined to one of 0.25 m. What is the total length?
A pencil costs ₹2.50 and an eraser ₹3.75. What is the total cost?
A bottle holds 1.5 L. Riya drinks 0.5 L. How much is left?
